units.citation: Rowland et al. (2026). Identifying predictors of tropical cyclone impacts on coastal agriculture to assess coastal wetland buffering signals. Journal of Applied Ecology.
units.quote:
Our analysis showed that croplands within 1 km of mangroves and tidal marshes 
experienced lower surface water presence and reduced crop cover declines 
compared with more distant areas.

relationship.outcome_raw: post-cyclone surface water presence on cropland (satellite water index, a proxy for flooding that does not separate surge from rain flooding), lower close to existing mangroves and tidal marshes than further away

context.practice_as_described: existing coastal wetlands — 'mangrove forests and tidal marshes' (aggregated, not separable) — adjacent to croplands; no restoration measured; the authors draw implications for restoration

relationship.outcome_raw: stream discharge during drought periods (antecedent-adjusted flow) across catchments, after vs before drain blocking: flows higher and recession slower

Higher flows persisted through droughts; slower recession only in the first 3 days (p13, Fig. 4). This is low-flow / drought-period yield, NOT annual yield: average flows DECLINE after blocking (see ev_water_yield_wils11db_3).

context.note: Modelled (PHYSITEL/HYDROTEL semi-distributed model, calibrated per sub-watershed, 47 climate projections, 1979-2099). Effects are reported as compensation trajectories (Fig. 4) and restoration targets (20 to 150% more wetland), not as a flow-change magnitude in the text, so no magnitude is encoded. The outcome is the natural logarithm of household income in Yuan (plus 1), so an ATT is a log difference and is read here as a log response ratio. units.citation: Wu et al. (2023). Wetland-based solutions against extreme flood and severe drought: Efficiency evaluation of risk mitigation. Climate Risk Management.
units.quote:
(i) quantify the impacts of wetlands on extreme flood and severe drought and (2) 
investigate the influences of geographical location and types of wetlands on their regulation ef­
ficiency. The hydrological modeling was conducted with various wetland loss scenarios on the 
Nenjiang River Basin (NRB)- a large river basin where wetlands are abundant and play an 
important hydrological regulation function. Modeling results showed that RWs mainly decreased

volume and slightly mitigated peak flow in the entire NRB. For severe drought, RWs overall
